sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Home Hydroponics and Gardening Equipment

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: federal common law for federal matters; Quebec civil law for private commercial law and partnership legal publicity
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between Canada and the European Union
Convention Between Canada and the United States with Respect to Taxes on Income and on Capital, as amended
OECD Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures to Prevent Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (MLI)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17, as amended; Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; An Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1 (including Division IV.1 on ultimate beneficiaries); Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46; Excise Tax Act, RSC 1985, c E-15; FINTRAC AML/CFT guidance and Canadian sanctions consolidated lists.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport or national identity card
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority or notary public in the partner's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the originating state is a Contracting Party; otherwise Consular Legalization at the Canadian embassy or high commission in the issuing state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of status, certificate of incumbency, or registry extract for any corporate general or limited partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry or company agent in the partner's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the originating registry is in an Apostille Convention state; otherwise Consular Legalization through the Canadian diplomatic mission having jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Legalized power of attorney appointing the proposed general partner or Quebec registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent authority in the originating jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the originating state is a Contracting Party; otherwise Consular Legalization at the Canadian embassy or high commission

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all partners, directors, and authorized representatives against the Canadian Consolidated Autonomous Sanctions List, United Nations Security Council sanctions, and publicly known enforcement lists; foreign politically exposed persons, heads of state, and heads of international organizations require enhanced due diligence under Part 1.1 of the PCMLTFA and FINTRAC guidance; domestic PEPs are also subject to enhanced CDD when establishing ongoing business relations; although OFAC screening is not strictly mandated by Canadian federal law, it is applied as institutional best practice where payment rails such as Stripe and PayPal are used.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — Registre des entreprises du Québec (REQ), accessible online at registraire.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The limited partnership name must be in French under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11; the legal designation must include 'société en commandite' or the abbreviation 'S.E.C.'; names from non-Latin alphabets must be transliterated into standard Latin characters using recognized French-Canadian transliteration conventions.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Any term implying or reserving government authority, including 'Canada', 'Quebec', 'Quebec', 'Regie', 'Ministere', 'Gouvernement', or municipal designations
Terms protected by professional and financial statutes, including 'banque', 'bank', 'assurance', 'insurance', 'fiducie', 'trust', 'universite', 'college', 'ordre', 'royal', and 'souverain'
Corporate designators inconsistent with limited partnership status, including 'Inc.', 'Ltd.', 'Corp.', 'Corporation', 'LLC', and 'S.A.'
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: There is no statutory extension of the initial 30-day reservation; a new name reservation request must be filed after expiry. If the name is rejected, the applicant may submit a written reconsideration request to the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec within 30 days of the notice, accompanied by amended arguments or a revised name. If the refusal is maintained, judicial review may be sought before the Cour du Quebec within the applicable delay prescribed by the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises and the Code of Civil Procedure.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office services are generally permissible for this ISIC 4791 online retail business, provided a real street address in Quebec is designated for service of process and the address is recorded in the REQ; a post office box alone is not sufficient. Payment processors and financial institutions may, however, require a physical operating address for underwriting.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low, estimated at under 5% per year for a Low_Risk_Standard online retail entity; the likelihood rises to 15% to 20% if there are material filing irregularities, significant payment-pattern anomalies, or identification of a PEP or sanctioned counterparty during beneficial ownership review.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name research and reservation fee with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Regulation respecting the publicity of enterprises

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Declaration of registration (immatriculation) for a societe en commandite (limited partnership)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff in the Registrar's published fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: French-language name clearance and statutory declaration drafting by a Quebec notary or attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Quebec notary or attorney in private practice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market fixed fee; not a statutory tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization and certified translation of partner KYC documents, approximate for three documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent foreign apostille authority and certified translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Foreign governmental fee plus prevailing market translation fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Quebec registered office and professional agent services, first year
AML/CFT compliance program setup, including UBO analysis, sanctions screening, and risk assessment

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec, articles 2236–2251 (limited partnership / société en commandite); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, ss. 10, 19–25 (registration and declaration requirements)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Quebec Enterprise Registrar
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for registration of a limited partnership / Déclaration d'immatriculation d'une société en commandite
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Quebec limited partnership; capital contributions are fixed in the partnership agreement. No escrow account is required under Quebec law for this non-financial, non-regulated activity.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: This written resolution is adopted by the general partner of [LP Name], a Quebec limited partnership (the “Partnership”), as the sole governing authority in lieu of a board of directors, under the Civil Code of Québec. 1. The Partnership accepts the subscription of the initial limited partner for the number of partnership units specified in the partnership agreement, and all capital contributions are credited upon deposit. 2. The registered office is fixed at [complete street address], Montreal, Quebec, and the general partner is directed to file the declaration of registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec. 3. [Name] is appointed general partner manager with authority to execute e-commerce agreements, open banking accounts, and comply with Revenu Québec and CRA registration obligations. Effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name search and optional name reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) online name-search and reservation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed limited partnership name through the REQ online portal, verify availability against the Quebec enterprise register, and pay any applicable reservation fee. For a société en commandite, the name must not be misleading and must comply with the name rules under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.
required_dossiers: Proposed limited partnership name
General partner identity document
Description of principal business activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or marked non-available, amend the proposed name on the REQ portal and resubmit; no formal appeal is needed until final refusal, in which case reconsideration may be requested from the Registrar or judicial review sought in the Superior Court of Quebec.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute limited partnership agreement and general partner consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel / notary as applicable; no public authority filing at this step
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute a written limited partnership agreement non the Civil Code of Québec, setting out capital contributions, profit-sharing, management powers of the general partner, limited partner restrictions, and dissolution events. The agreement should be signed by all general and limited partners; notarization is advisable if real property is contributed, but is not mandatory for standard e-commerce and warehousing operations.
required_dossiers: Limited partnership agreement
General partner written consent and undertaking
Limited partner subscription forms and capital contribution records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the partnership agreement is defective, amend the agreement by written consent of all partners and restate the subscription documents before filing the declaration of registration with the REQ.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File declaration of registration with the Registraire des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — online enterprise registration service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the application for registration of the limited partnership through the REQ online portal. Provide the partnership name, registered office address in Quebec, general partner and limited partner information, and statutory declarations. Submit the required dossiers electronically or by mail. Upon approval, the REQ will assign the enterprise number (NEQ) and issue a certificate of registration.
required_dossiers: Completed application for registration form
Certified copy of the limited partnership agreement
Notarized declaration or attestation if required
Identity and address information for all general partners and limited partners
Registered office address proof
Authorization from the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is refused or queried, correct the discrepancies identified by the REQ in the application and resubmit online or by letter. If the refusal continues, the general partner may file a written request for the Registrar's reconsideration or apply to the Superior Court of Quebec for a declaration regarding the sufficiency of the registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) and register for tax accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec; Revenu Québec; Canada Revenue Agency (CRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the REQ issues the NEQ, register the limited partnership with Revenu Québec for Quebec Sales Tax (QST) and GST/QST harmonization, payroll source deductions if employees will be hired, and any applicable corporate taxes. Obtain a federal business number (BN) from the CRA through the Business Registration Online service.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration issued by REQ
NEQ number
Limited partnership agreement and partner list
General partner information and governance documents
Expected revenue and registration start date
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a tax account registration is delayed or rejected, contact Revenu Québec and the CRA directly to reconcile missing data, provide additional proof of the limited partnership's existence, and resubmit the registration through the respective online portals.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt operational governance resolutions and open business bank accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General partner; chartered bank or financial institution; payment processors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt an operational resolution appointing a managing person and authorizing the opening of bank accounts, execution of payment processor agreements (e.g. Stripe, PayPal), and signing of e-commerce marketplace contracts. Submit the registration documents and KYC information to the bank and payment processors.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration from REQ
Limited partnership agreement
Operational resolution of the general partner
Identification and beneficial ownership declarations for banking and AML compliance
Business address and e-commerce platform details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank or payment processor queries the KYC package, supplement with a certified copy of the REQ registration, a notarized identity documents, and a detailed organizational chart of the general partner; if the issue persists, select an alternative financial institution or payment processor.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie (MEIE) does not require an industrial manufacturing licence for this e-commerce distribution-only activity
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required — online retail of home hydroponics and gardening equipment is not a regulated manufacturing or industrial activity in Quebec

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no environmental impact assessment report is required for warehousing and online retail distribution; administrative exemption applies under the Regulation respecting environmental impact assessment and review
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — no industrial wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste streams are generated from warehousing and e-commerce fulfilment; compliance with municipal waste sorting, packaging, and electronic-waste disposal rules remains required

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Municipal building/occupancy permit and fire-safety certificate for any commercial warehouse or office; compliance with CNESST occupational health and safety rules; no special civil-defence clearance or industrial works permit is required for online retail of hydroponics equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada - Federal tax administration; principal portal: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html). In Quebec, Revenu Québec administers provincial tax registration and the Quebec Sales Tax (QST).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident limited partnership must first apply to CRA for a Business Number (BN) with a GST/HST program account (RT), using Form RC1 or through My Business Account. For Quebec provincial sales tax (QST), the partnership must register with Revenu Québec via Form LM-1-V or the online Quebec business registration portal, obtaining a QST number (ND). Supporting documents typically include: the LP declaration / partnership agreement, foreign registration extract, proof of non-resident status, a valid power of attorney or authorization, banking information, and, where applicable, a Canadian representative for service of process. Registration is mandatory before making taxable supplies unless the small-supplier threshold is not exceeded.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A Canadian limited partnership is fiscally transparent for income tax purposes; allocations of income and loss are made in accordance with subsection 96(1) of the Income Tax Act. There is no US-style check-the-box election available. A partner may elect under subsection 97(2) to transfer property to the partnership on a rollover basis. Hybrid mismatch rules (sections 18.2 and 18.3 of the Income Tax Act) restrict the deduction or inclusion treatment of hybrid arrangements involving partnerships and hybrid instruments.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) / Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) - Quebec Sales Tax (QST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in taxable supplies in the preceding four calendar quarters (or the current quarter if carrying on commercial activity in Canada); the Quebec QST registration threshold is aligned at CAD 30,000 under the same small-supplier exemption.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time e-invoicing, fiscal clearance, or digital stamping regime applies in Canada at the federal or Quebec level for standard online retail. Electronic invoices in PDF/EDI formats are valid if they meet the integrity and traceability requirements stated in CRA Information Circular IC 106-6R. Quebec has certain sector-specific digital reporting obligations (e.g., accommodation platforms), but none are applicable to hydroponics equipment e-commerce. Registered businesses must retain all invoicing and export records for at least six years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Tangible personal property, including garden hydroponics equipment, is zero-rated under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act when the supplier sells to a non-resident recipient and the goods are exported from Canada as part of the supply, or when delivered to a common carrier for export. The supply must not be conditioned on use in Canada, and documentary proof of export must be obtained. Services directly related to the exported goods (e.g., logistics, installation or assembly outside Canada) may also be zero-rated. Digital supplies delivered electronically to a non-resident purchaser may qualify as zero-rated services when the recipient is outside Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (submitted through CBSA's Canadian Export Reporting System/eManifest or Form B13A as applicable)
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / Truck Waybill showing the carrier, consignee, and export destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank / payment processor settlement statement evidencing receipt of foreign consideration
Commercial Invoice / Sales Contract referencing the exported goods and purchase order
Packing list and HS/ISIC classification documentation substantiating the nature of the goods
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess a zero-rated export within the normal four-year limitation period; the period is unlimited in cases of false statements, misrepresentation, or fraud. A false export zero-rating claim attracts penalties under section 280 of the Excise Tax Act of up to 100% of the net tax deficiency, plus arrears interest. Criminal tax evasion prosecution can result in fines up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment. Exporters must retain contemporaneous export evidence for six years; failure to do so triggers reversal of the zero-rating, additional GST/QST assessment, and clawback of input tax credits.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), with foreign exchange and anti-money laundering reporting oversight also exercised by the Department of Finance Canada and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a liberalized and fully convertible currency regime without exchange controls. Both capital and current account transactions are freely permitted, and there are no restrictions on the repatriation of capital or profits for qualified non-resident investors. Profit remittance hurdles are primarily tax-driven rather than regulatory: dividends or partnership distributions to non-residents are generally subject to Canadian non-resident withholding tax under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act, typically 25% absent an applicable income tax treaty, with treaty rates frequently reduced to 5%–15% for direct and indirect interests. For a Quebec Limited Partnership, careful characterization of distributions as return of capital versus allocated income is essential to optimize withholding and treaty eligibility. The Bank of Canada does not impose prior approval, surrender, or conversion mandates, but Canadian financial institutions require proper source-of-funds documentation and beneficial ownership disclosure for all cross-border transfers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada has no export proceeds surrender requirement, no statutory repatriation timeline, and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. Exporters are free to hold, use, or remit foreign currency proceeds subject only to standard commercial banking arrangements and FINTRAC threshold reporting. For goods sold online, export documentation such as commercial invoices, customs declarations, and shipping evidence must be retained for tax and audit purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium with legal constraints. Offshore digital EMI platforms (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex) can be used as supplementary payment corridors for cross-border receipts and disbursements, but they are not licensed as Canadian banks and cannot provide full domestic clearing or CDIC-insured deposit services. Any entity providing payment services in Canada is typically required to register as a Money Services Business (MSB) with FINTRAC and comply with the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act. Reliance on a non-Canadian EMI as the primary treasury account is discouraged due to limited regulatory comfort, potential KYC friction, and insufficient credit facilities. A dual-rail structure with a Canadian chartered bank as the principal account and an EMI as a settlement accelerator is operationally viable.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Quebec Limited Partnership with non-resident partners or directors, a physical presence for at least one senior partner, authorized signatory, or director is generally required at account opening at tier-1 Canadian banks, especially for non-Canadian directors. Remote opening is permissible on a case-by-case basis for Canadian residents using notarized identification and video verification, but cross-border structures normally trigger institutional policy requiring an in-branch interview or a Canadian registered agent to attest identities. Banks in Quebec may also require a valid Quebec enterprise registration (NEQ) and a partnership agreement or declaration of registration from the Registraire des entreprises.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Hydroponics and gardening equipment flagged as a potential cannabis cultivation vector
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a written business plan expressly excluding cannabis, a copy of the ISIC 4791 and NAICS 444220 classification certificate, product catalogue, vendor agreements, customer onboarding due diligence, and a compliance policy prohibiting sales to illegal processors. Include certifications that products are for legitimate legal horticultural use only.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partners causing uncertainty in beneficial ownership and source of funds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver organizational documents, certificate of limited partnership, register of partners, partnership agreement, passport copies, proof of address, reference letters from source banks, and a source-of-wealth statement for each non-resident underlying beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Online retail model with dispersed cross-border counterparties creating higher transaction reconciliation risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present audited merchant statements, payment processor reports from Stripe/PayPal, warehouse and logistics invoices, refund policy, and a transaction monitoring program. Provide a chart of expected monthly volume and demonstrate clear segregation of client funds and operational accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential exposure to dual-use goods or export-controlled merchandise
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Include export classification classification, harmonized system codes, confirmation from Global Affairs Canada that the goods are not controlled, and existing export permits or exemptions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injections from non-resident partners or parent entities are executed via SWIFT MT103 transfers to the Canadian LP's capital escrow or operational account at a Canadian chartered bank. Reference must clearly state 'Limited Partnership Capital Contribution' and, where applicable, 'Foreign Direct Investment'. Canadian banks may require supporting documents such as the partnership agreement, the board or partner resolution authorizing the capital call, and a declaration of source of funds. No exchange control approval is required, but wire transfers exceeding CAD 10,000 are reportable to FINTRAC. For statistical reporting to Statistics Canada, the transaction may be classified as a direct investment equity liability. Settlement is typically in CAD, with conversion from USD or EUR handled at the receiving bank's commercial rate or via a pre-agreed client FX forward.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound supplier and trade payments are cleared primarily through SWIFT MT103 for direct correspondent banking transfers, especially for international suppliers. For high-value or repeat bulk purchases, commercial letters of credit (documentary credits confirmed by the Canadian bank) provide secure payment against shipping and inspection documents. Domestic suppliers are settled via EFT/Interac or wire transfer. For cross-border disbursements, the bank will require an underlying invoice, purchase order, and in certain cases a certificate of origin for tariff classification. Currency conversion on outbound payments is executed at spot or via a booked forward, with SWIFT payment details containing the applicable corporate purpose code or descriptive payment narrative aligning with the goods sold and ISIC 4791 classification.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign exchange forward contracts with Canadian chartered banks
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for non-convertible or restricted emerging-market currencies
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for long-term CAD/USD exposure
Plain vanilla foreign exchange options (call and put) for downside protection

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under An Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually during the calendar month containing the initial registration anniversary; due no later than the last day of that anniversary month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a CAD 60 late-fee notice; failure to file for two consecutive years exposes the partnership to administrative strike-off from the REQ registry and subsequent loss of legal-publicity protection for partners.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return (Federal partnership tax filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than six months after the partnership fiscal year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, due by June 30 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file imposes CAD 10 per partner per day for up to 100 days, with a maximum aggregate penalty of CAD 2,000 under Income Tax Act section 162(7); separate penalties apply for failing to furnish partner copies.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory compulsory audit applies to a Quebec limited partnership under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. Compulsory engagement may be triggered by the partnership agreement, a third-party lender covenant, a corporate general partner's securities-law reporting obligations, or an CRA verification order; the CRA does not impose a numeric audit threshold for a small e-commerce LP.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: CPA Canada Handbook accounting framework: IFRS for public-reporting entities; ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) for private Canadian entities. A non-listed e-commerce limited partnership ordinarily uses ASPE, unless the partnership agreement or a financial institution requires IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no separate federal beneficial-ownership attestation regime for a Quebec limited partnership. UBO identity and percentage ownership are part of the annual REQ declaration. Any transfer or issuance of partnership units that changes the UBO portion must be declared to REQ within 60 days after the event; the annual anniversary declaration thereafter confirms the current UBO schedule. The general partner remains responsible for maintaining a partner ledger and documenting limits on transfer.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners and General Partner(s)
Register of Partnership Interest Transfers and Allocations
Partnership Resolution Book (Consents and Written Resolutions)
Record of Registered Office in Quebec and Agent (if any)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 180 - USD 540 (CAD 240 - CAD 730) depending on registered-office services or Quebec representation agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 15,000 only if a full certified audit is contractually required; no quantum applies to the standard annual CRA/REQ compliance cycle

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined statutory corporate rate for corporate partners (15% federal general rate + 11.5% Quebec general rate). The Quebec Limited Partnership itself is fiscally transparent and pays no entity-level income tax; income flows through to partners. A Quebec-resident individual partner faces a combined top marginal rate of approximately 53.31% on allocated active business income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No entity-level income tax applies to the LP. Flow-through incentives available to qualifying partners: SR&ED refundable investment tax credits (35% for CCPCs); Quebec E-Business tax credit for online retail and digital commerce; reduced taxation for qualified intellectual property income under the federal patent box regime; and the Small Business Deduction (federal 9% + Quebec 3% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income) where a corporate partner is a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) allocating partnership business income. Non-resident partners may further reduce Part XIII withholding and branch tax through applicable tax treaties.
